sacha: Ecuadorian Taxonomic and Ethnobotanical Data Toolkit

Source: R/sacha-package.R
sacha-package.Rd

Tools to resolve scientific names, retrieve taxonomic classification, conservation status, common names, sustainable-use records, and cross-platform indexation URLs from local ColDP archives and web services (ChecklistBank / Catalogue of Life, GBIF, iNaturalist); to build occurrence maps; and to emit all of the above as markdown-formatted text ready for inclusion in a report.

Package modules

  • coldp – accessors reading a local ColDP archive (sacha_coldp_configure(), sc_full_name_coldp(), etc.).

  • core – web-backed accessors querying ChecklistBank, GBIF, and iNaturalist directly (sacha_configure(), sc_full_name(), classification(), etc.).

  • spatial – GBIF occurrence maps and Catalogue of Life geographic locations (gbif_map(), col_locations()).

  • inaturalist – iNaturalist observation images, local archiving, and markdown-formatted figure panels (inat_images(), inat_save_images()).

Documenting plain / _md twin functions

Many accessors ship in pairs: a plain-text version and a _md (Markdown) version intended for use inside a rendered report. Whether a pair shares one help page or gets two follows a single rule:

  • If the _md twin has an identical signature to its plain counterpart and differs only in output format, document both together with a shared @rdname (see the coldp module for the canonical example).

  • If the _md twin introduces its own parameters (e.g. fig_width, fig_height in gbif_map_md()) and/or diverges in error-handling contract (e.g. a communication failure is silenced in the _md variant but raised as an error in the plain one, as in col_locations() vs. col_locations_md()), document them on separate pages instead.

Never force a shared @rdname onto a pair that fails either check – a page whose Usage section lists two mismatched signatures, or whose Value section has to describe two different error contracts, is harder to read than two short separate pages.

Documenting one-line wrapper families

A family of thin wrappers around one underlying function (e.g. the *_url accessors – ipni_url(), gbif_url(), col_url(), etc. – all delegating to indexations()) should share a single @rdname page with one @param/@return/@examples block and a @details table mapping each function name to what it fixes (e.g. its identifier). Each wrapper keeps its own @export; only the documentation is consolidated.

Avoiding duplicated @param blocks

When two non-twin functions share most of their parameters but return different things or have different side effects (e.g. inat_images(), which returns an object, vs. inat_save_images(), which writes files to disk), do not repeat the shared @param entries. Use @inheritParams <reference_function> and document only the parameters that are genuinely specific to the function at hand.

Language resolution

Every module resolves its language argument dynamically against the .yml files shipped under inst/lang/: any file inst/lang/<code>.yml (plus any aliases: it declares) becomes a valid language value without changing any R code. Do not hardcode a closed set such as language = c("es", "en") with match.arg() in new code – that silently breaks this extensibility contract. If a module currently does this, it is a known inconsistency to be fixed, not a pattern to copy.
